Hi Maria — Laura Bennett from Redwood legal. Thanks for the clear list. A few practical notes on audit scope and evidence exchange so procurement has clarity for contract terms: 

- SOC 2 / Reports: we will provide the latest SOC 2 Type II and our penetration test summary under an NDA. These cover controls, control periods, and remediation notes.
- Audit rights: Redwood supports reasonable audit activities but we carve a predictable process into the DPA: 30 days' notice for on-site or expanded remote evidence requests; audits limited to inspection of controls relevant to the processing of GreenMed data; customer auditors must sign our standard NDA and not perform disruptive testing.
- Remote evidence: for many customers we provide a remote evidence pack (logs, configuration snapshots, policy documents) and a 4-hour working session with our engineers. 
- Third-party auditors: allowed with prior consent and an engagement letter; we may require a narrow scoping addendum and a limiter on data access.
- Redlines: if GreenMed requires broader audit rights than above (e.g., continuous monitoring or real-time access to logs), we will need to negotiate appropriate security and cost mitigations.

Kim identified the attachments we can share. To help procurement, here's suggested contract language (high level) you can include in the DPA: 

"Customer will have the right to perform an audit of Processor's controls relevant to the Services, subject to Processor's standard audit procedures, 30 days' prior written notice, execution of Processor's NDA, and scope limited to the processing of Customer Data."

If you want legal to review specific language, please share any proposed DPA redlines and we'll respond within 3 business days.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Transfer mechanisms: we support EU SCCs for data transfers (we offer executed SCCs as part of the DPA). For any transfers that require additional mitigations we perform a Transfer Impact Assessment — summary provided in the attached TIA doc.
